output.name: Tormesk

anatomy.part: stern post, top of the long boat
stern foot, where the hull curves under
forward keel, low on the hull
keel amidships, the deepest point of the hull
prow tip, raised at the right
thwart lamp on the gunwale amidships, the brightest light in the boat
masthead light at the top of the sail
top of the aft oar, lifted above the water
blade of that oar, the last trace of a rower's hand

output.myth: Eleven rowers took a long boat out past the last light, because Tavo laughed at them and they were proud. The wind came round behind them and the boat would not turn for any prayer. So they rowed on in the dark. With each stroke one of them let go of a name: first the one his mother used at the hearth, then the one his wife used, then the one that meant brave. The water took them one at a time as payment for the crossing. Only the oars were left, because the sea does not want oars. Mother Hesk counted them at the Reel and wrote eleven in her book, though no one can say who they were. Kael still casts his net for them and never catches one. If you find yourself rowing past your own name, do not turn to look for it. Count your strokes instead, and you will get home, though you will be known by the number.
output.verse:
Eleven oars, blind
the names went under the sea
Hesk keeps count. Row on.
